correctness.rationale: Vertices are precisely lifts of nonzero zero divisors of the chain quotient, so valuation layers give \(N=s(q^{k-1}-1)\) and the nonzero socle lifts have size \(m=s(q-1)\). Every socle lift is universal. For \(k\ge3\), a valuation-one vertex has open neighborhood exactly the socle-lift set, forcing every total dominating set to meet it; for \(k=2\) that set is all vertices. Meeting the universal set together with cardinality at least two is also sufficient. The generating polynomial and minimum-pair count are then exact subset counts. Every admissible two-set is an edge, so it is paired. The \(N=1\) case is the isolated vertex. The inspected verifier independently reconstructs several quotient multiplication tables and matches all coefficients.
correctness.risk: The theorem requires a finite chain-ring quotient; higher-dimensional socles need not satisfy the same one-layer forcing.

value.rationale: The result upgrades a minimum-number observation to a complete, fibre-sensitive enumeration for a natural ring-theoretic graph family and simultaneously determines every minimum paired dominating set. The socle-lift forcing gives the algebraic reason for the closed polynomial.
value.risk: After the socle forcing lemma is isolated, the final subset counting is elementary.

final_claim: If \(R/I\) is a finite chain ring with residue-field order \(q\), nilpotency length \(k\ge2\), and \(s=|I|\), put \(N=s(q^{k-1}-1)\) and \(m=s(q-1)\). A subset of the ideal-based zero-divisor graph is total dominating exactly when it has at least two vertices and meets the \(m\) lifts of the nonzero socle. Hence \(D_t(x)=(1+x)^N-(1+x)^{N-m}-mx\); when \(N\ge2\), total and paired domination have minimum two and the minimum pairs are exactly the two-subsets meeting that socle-lift set.
limitations: The quotient \(R/I\) must be a finite chain ring.
The one-vertex boundary has no total or paired dominating set.
